scope_note: Two-pass project-scoped audit of Stream Data Centers Houston I / IAHA1 at 4001 Technology Forest Boulevard under worker-research-contract 2.0.0. The governed project is the single facility represented by IM3 point 09190480200 and exact parcel 9714-07-00103; broader Stream portfolios, the separate 4000 Technology Forest data-center project, later capacity changes, tenant deployments and equipment, and company-wide activities are excluded unless explicitly retained as unallocated context. Reported observations, source forecasts and modeled syntheses remain separate; no modeled synthesis passed the project-specific eligibility gate.

sources.title: Stream Data Centers commissions Houston-area Private Data Center
sources.publisher: Stream Data Centers via PR Newswire
sources.notes: The dated operator announcement says construction began in August 2012 and construction and commissioning were complete by June 11, 2013. It reports the exact facility as a 74,901-square-foot ground-up development with 30,000 square feet of raised floor delivering 3.375 MW of commissioned critical load, expandable to 6.75 MW. The expandable rating is not treated as commissioned capacity, electricity use or investment; the release discloses no project cost, construction labor, operating headcount, payroll, tax incentive or public cost.

sources.title: Houston I IAHA1 data center specification sheet
sources.notes: Pages 1-2 identify IAHA1, also called Houston I, at 4001 Technology Forest Boulevard. The current sheet reports a 74,901-square-foot facility, three 10,000-square-foot data halls, and a design supporting 7.8 MW of 2N critical load, with dual underground utility feeds and air-cooled chillers. The 7.8 MW value is a current engineering capacity rating, not a meter, occupied load, annual electricity, generator output, water use or a monetary contribution.

sources.title: Houston I - The Woodlands current facility page
sources.notes: The current operator page identifies Houston I at 4001 Technology Forest Boulevard, marks capacity available, reports 1.1 MW immediately available and says the site has operated since 2013. Available capacity is not total commissioned or occupied load. References to Houston-area market conditions, other Stream campuses, public-cloud providers and renewable-energy incentives are not allocated to this facility.

sources.title: Winter Storm Uri data center performance and energy program update
sources.notes: The operator reports that H-1 in The Woodlands lost utility power for approximately 15 hours during Winter Storm Uri, that backup systems performed as designed and service was not disrupted, and that the facility was served by Entergy. The document contains no meter, kWh, peak demand, bill, fuel volume, generator runtime by unit, outage cost or project-specific Foundation payment.

sources.title: Stream Data Centers and Crown Castle bring new fiber into The Woodlands
sources.notes: The exact-facility announcement identifies Crown Castle as a new fiber provider at Houston I and describes almost 75,000 square feet of purpose-built space. It establishes a supplier relationship and continued operation but reports no contract value, invoice, local labor, supplier residence, procurement share or public infrastructure payment.

sources.title: Montgomery County Clerk official records search
sources.notes: Index and OCR searches covered January 1, 2011 through September 1, 2026 using IP Stream Houston, IP Stream Houston REIT, Stream Data Centers, Woodlands Industrial Development, 4001 Technology Forest, 4001 Research Forest, parcel 9714-07-00103 and tax account 0097140700103. The portal exposed no document image or consideration that could be verified as facility acquisition price, project debt, lien amount, lease payment or public obligation; an index result alone cannot establish economic value or project incidence.

sources.title: IP Stream Houston REIT, LLC Form D
sources.notes: The filing reports a $115,000 equity offering sold by IP Stream Houston REIT, LLC, with proceeds for working capital. The filing does not identify 4001 Technology Forest Boulevard, IP Stream Houston LLC, a property acquisition, capital expenditure or facility use of proceeds, so the offering is not treated as project investment or supplier spend.

sources.title: Texas Architectural Barriers online project search
sources.publisher: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
sources.notes: The project portal and indexed project pages were searched across 2011-2026 for 4001 Technology Forest, Stream Data Centers, IP Stream Houston, Houston I and Private Data Center in Montgomery County. No matching Houston I project detail, estimated construction cost, inspection or design-firm record surfaced. TABS2022003527 is an $8,967,629 alteration at the distinct 4000 Technology Forest Boulevard data center and is excluded rather than assigned to Houston I.

sources.title: Texas registered qualifying data centers list
sources.notes: The complete registered qualifying and qualifying-large-project lists were searched for Stream, IP Stream, Houston I, IAHA1, 4001 Technology Forest, Woodlands Industrial Development and known tenant T-Systems. No Houston I registration appears. The absence does not prove that no other tax treatment ever applied, but it supplies no basis for a state data-center sales-tax exemption amount or realized tax expenditure.

sources.title: Texas Local Development Agreement Search
sources.notes: Chapter 312, 380 and 381 searches used Montgomery County and The Woodlands local-government names with entity terms IP Stream Houston, Stream Data Centers, Houston I, 4001 Technology Forest and Woodlands Industrial Development. No matching agreement or attachment was returned. Coverage requirements emphasize agreements active as of September 1, 2021 or later-reported agreements, so a negative result cannot prove that no pre-2021 incentive existed.

sources.notes: The adopted budget, FY2023-FY2025 ACFR collection, Commissioners Court document index and monthly-auditor materials were searched for Stream, IP Stream, Technology Forest, data center, tax abatement, Chapter 381, TIRZ, infrastructure, fire, road, reimbursement, grant, bond and utility across available 2012-2026 documents. Aggregate economic-development payments and county service budgets were found, but no Houston I appropriation, reimbursement, bond, marginal service cost, recipient receipt or project-level public expenditure was identified.

sources.notes: Central Registry, permit-map and Central File Room pathways were searched by 4001 Technology Forest, 4001 Research Forest, IP Stream Houston, Stream Houston, Houston I, IAHA1 and Montgomery County for air, emergency-engine, petroleum-storage, industrial-waste, construction-stormwater, wastewater and water records across 2011-2026. sources.title: BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages data access
sources.notes: QCEW county files and the repository county panel were reviewed for Montgomery County, Texas, including total covered employment, average annual pay and NAICS 518/data-processing availability before and after 2013. Published county or industry aggregates cannot identify Stream, its tenants, contractors, worker residence or the selected facility, and disclosure suppression and changing county composition prevent a project payroll or causal employment/wage claim.

sources.title: BEA GDP by county data access and methodology
sources.notes: BEA county GDP files and the repository's 2001-2024 county history panel were reviewed for FIPS 48339. They describe the entire Montgomery County economy and do not isolate Stream, tenants or Houston I. The unresolved county-first-entry status, rapid population and industry change, simultaneous development, and absence of a validated comparator or treatment share prevent attribution of county GDP changes to this facility.

project_updates.title: Investment audit - no attributable project cost
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Stream operator history, commissioning release and current site materials; Montgomery CAD real and personal-property histories; County Clerk official-record index and OCR; SEC EDGAR; county budgets/ACFRs; Texas incentive databases; local reporting and archived project announcements. Queries covered Stream Data Centers, IP Stream Houston LLC, IP Stream Houston REIT LLC, Woodlands Industrial Development LLC, Houston I, H-1, IAHA1, 4001 Technology Forest, 4001 Research Forest, parcel 9714-07-00103 and tax accounts 0097140700103/P454338 across 2011-2026. Stream disclosed no construction cost in contemporary reporting; its generic greater-than-$1,000-per-square-foot comparison is not a project amount. The $115,000 REIT equity offering says working capital and lacks a facility crosswalk. Appraised-value stocks and property-tax payments are not capital expenditure, while deed consideration, acquisition price, audited capex, financing draw and tenant-equipment investment remain unresolved.
project_updates.project_description: Stream Data Centers' Houston I (IAHA1) is the single purpose-built data-center facility at 4001 Technology Forest Boulevard in The Woodlands, Montgomery County, Texas, not Stream's wider Houston or Texas portfolio or the separate 4000 Technology Forest project. Stream began construction in August 2012 and announced construction and commissioning complete on June 11, 2013; current operator materials say it has operated since 2013. The 74,901-square-foot facility contains three 10,000-square-foot data halls and commissioned 3.375 MW of critical load at opening; later tenant deployments, the current 7.8-MW design rating, tenant equipment and broader portfolio activity remain separately scoped.

project_updates.title: Construction audit - chronology only
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: TDLR Architectural Barriers project search, Montgomery County/Fire Marshal web and Commissioners Court document indexes, The Woodlands Township records, operator releases, OSHA establishment inspections, contractor/architect searches and contemporary local reporting. Searches used the exact address, aliases, legal entities, parcel/account identifiers, permit/inspection/occupancy terms and 2011-2026 dates. The operator fixes construction from August 2012 to commissioning on June 11, 2013, but no permit number, administrative valuation, certificate, impact/connection fee, contractor roster, construction worker count, hours, job-years, payroll or residence record was found. TABS2022003527 at 4000 Technology Forest is a distinct later project and its $8,967,629 cost is excluded.

project_updates.title: Supplier audit - identities without spend
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: operator specification and connectivity pages, Crown Castle announcement, carrier directories, procurement/vendor searches, County Clerk and Commissioners Court records, OSHA, contractor searches and local business reporting. Exact searches combined Houston I, H-1, IAHA1, Stream/IP Stream, 4001 Technology Forest and known provider names AT&T, Lumen/CenturyLink, Comcast, Crown Castle, Ezee Fiber, Fidium, Megaport and Tachus with contract, invoice, vendor, subcontractor, procurement, local spend and fiber. Crown Castle's 2020 installation and the operator's carrier list establish relationships only. No contract value, payment, complete supplier roster, supplier location, local-purchase share or non-overlap ledger was found; tenant and portfolio vendors are not allocated.

project_updates.title: Operations audit - scale and continuity only
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: current and archived operator facility pages, commissioning and storm materials, tenant certificates, Stream careers and job postings, Texas workforce sources, BLS QCEW, assessor accounts and local reporting. Searches used all project aliases, exact address, IP Stream/SDC Technology Services, operations, technician, payroll, wage, headcount, FTE, shift, benefits and tenant terms across 2013-2026. Direct records now preserve the exact 74,901-square-foot operating facility and capacity snapshots; current availability and a single technician vacancy do not establish employment stock. No facility headcount, annual FTE, payroll, benefits, occupation mix, residence, turnover, operating expense, revenue or tenant-versus-operator allocation was found.

project_updates.title: Fiscal audit - account payments remain controlling
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Montgomery CAD parcel 9714-07-00103 and personal-property account P454338, Tax Office accounts 0097140700103 and 1310000507453, payment histories, owner/legal-description changes, County budgets/ACFRs, taxing-unit and incentive records. The 46 existing reported actuals remain controlling: 12 annual real-property appraisal stocks, 12 real-property account payments, 11 separately scoped personal-property appraisal stocks and 11 personal-property account payments. The equipment account's older 4001 Research Forest description supports association but its missing displayed situs requires separation. Payments are not recipient-level receipts and do not identify remitter or incidence; no taxing-entity distribution, refund, delinquency, sales/franchise tax, fee, PILOT, net fiscal account or 2026 completed appraisal/payment was found.

project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Texas Chapters 312/380/381 Local Development Agreement Search, qualifying-data-center registry, Chapter 311/312 reports, Montgomery County FY2025 budget and FY2023-FY2025 ACFRs, Commissioners Court index, bond/debt resources, Tax Office accounts and public reporting. The registry's reporting window cannot prove no older incentive; generic county spending and statewide policies are not project costs and cannot be netted against multi-jurisdiction tax-account payments.

project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Stream Data Centers and Stream Realty community/news archives, Stream Support Foundation IRS filings and indexes, Montgomery County/Township agendas and budgets, recipient and nonprofit searches, and Houston/Woodlands local reporting. Searches combined Stream/IP Stream/Houston I/4001 Technology Forest with donation, grant, sponsorship, scholarship, training, school, nonprofit, fire, emergency, workforce and named-recipient terms across 2013-2026. The Foundation is company-wide and employee-focused; its filings provide no Houston I or Montgomery County allocation. Storm hotel support is not quantified or facility-attributed. project_updates.notes: Gap-closure searches returned to the County Clerk official index/OCR, SEC EDGAR, MCAD ownership history, operator history and web archives using IP Stream Houston LLC, IP Stream Houston REIT LLC, Stream Data Centers, SDC Technology Services LLC, Woodlands Industrial Development LLC, exact addresses, parcel/account numbers, deed, sale, mortgage, lien, UCC, lease, REIT and litigation. The 2016 Form D is working capital and not a facility investment. MCAD's 2026 owner-name change does not establish consideration or an operating transfer. project_updates.title: Permit, incentive, infrastructure and public-record gap closure
project_updates.notes: Gap closure used alternate official repositories after thin address indexing: TDLR statewide project search, Texas Comptroller qualifying-data-center and local-agreement databases, TCEQ Central Registry/permit-map/Central File Room routes, County Clerk OCR, Montgomery County public.destinyhosted.com Commissioners Court files, county budget/ACFR PDFs and operator archives. No matching original permit, inspection/certificate number, agreement attachment, compliance audit, environmental authorization, infrastructure payment, public grant or project-level cost surfaced. Portal absence is recorded as an unresolved gap, not evidence of zero.

project_updates.title: Workforce, contractor, supplier and recipient gap closure
project_updates.notes: Gap closure returned to OSHA by entity/address/ZIP and likely-contractor terms, Stream careers and archived vacancies, Texas/BLS workforce data, operator and carrier releases, IRS filings, recipient-side searches and County/Township records. One current engineering-technician vacancy cannot be converted to headcount, and no exact-site OSHA record identifies a builder. Crown Castle is a verified supplier identity without a payment. The company-wide Foundation and tenant T-Systems records do not allocate jobs, payroll, purchases or gifts to Houston I. Construction workforce, operating FTE/payroll, contractor payments, local supplier retention, apprenticeship/training and recipient-confirmed community support remain unresolved.

project_updates.title: Candidate-by-candidate modeling and county-outcome decision
project_updates.notes: Metric-specific eligibility review after both direct-evidence passes. Investment: rejected - appraisals are stocks, the Form D is unlinked working capital and no capex/acquisition base exists. Construction: rejected - no permit valuation, payroll, hours, contractor spend or project/local labor coefficient exists. Suppliers: rejected - identities without payments, vendor geography or a bounded local share cannot support output. Operations: rejected - floor area/capacity cannot generate FTE, payroll, revenue or operating expense, and a vacancy is not headcount. Fiscal: rejected - summing real and separately associated personal-property payments would add no decision-useful fact and still would not produce recipient receipts or incidence. Public costs: rejected - a tax-equal break-even identity would merely restate multi-jurisdiction payments without observed county cost, while no incentive or infrastructure expenditure exists. Resources: rejected - converting 3.375/7.8 MW design capacity through assumed utilization, uptime or PUE would invent electricity; water, fuel and emissions inputs are absent. Community: rejected - no project gift or recipient base exists. County employment: rejected - QCEW aggregates cannot identify Stream/tenant/contractor workers, county first entry is unresolved and no validated counterfactual or treatment share exists. County wages: rejected - composition change is not project payroll and the same identification failures apply. County GDP: rejected - BEA county output spans a rapidly changing, diversified county with concurrent development and no defensible comparator or facility allocation. Modeled additions: zero; forecasts added: zero. All unresolved metrics remain gaps rather than arbitrary shares, transferred multipliers, capacity conversions or unsupported causal effects.
